title: ETH barrier to single-exponential treewidth computation
formal: Assuming the deterministic Exponential-Time Hypothesis (ETH) defined below, is an exact single-exponential parameterized algorithm for Treewidth impossible? Specifically, let \(\mathrm{FastTW}\) mean that there exist a deterministic Turing machine \(A\), constants \(C\ge1\), and integers \(a,b\ge1\) such that, for every simple undirected graph \(G\) on \(n\ge1\) vertices and every integer \(0\le k<n\), \(A(G,k)\) decides whether \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\le k\) correctly within \(C\,2^{ak}(n+2)^b\) steps. Under the assumption ETH, determine whether \(\neg\mathrm{FastTW}\) or \(\mathrm{FastTW}\) holds. This selects the explicit single-exponential example in the source’s broader request for lower bounds.
why: Treewidth is a central measure of how close a graph is to a tree, and a decomposition is often the prerequisite for running efficient parameterized algorithms. The cost of finding the optimum can therefore dominate the cost of using the structure. Establishing whether a single-exponential dependence is compatible with ETH would locate a major boundary between structural preprocessing and algorithms that work once a decomposition is already known.
status_note: The 2014 source explicitly asks whether ETH excludes a single-exponential parameterized exact algorithm. The checked 2023 upper bound has quadratic parameter dependence in the exponent, while Bonnet’s 2025/2026 lower bound excludes subexponential dependence but not single-exponential dependence. Bounded checks through 2026-09-15 did not locate a resolution of this remaining conditional question.

progress.text: Bodlaender poses the explicit ETH question about exact single-exponential parameter dependence in Seminar 14451, Section 4.7, printed page 18.
Korhonen and Lokshtanov’s STOC 2023 result gives exact treewidth in \(2^{O(k^2)}n^{O(1)}\) time. The checked arXiv version 2 is dated 17 August 2023.

Bonnet’s arXiv version 2 proves the ETH-tight exponential lower bound in the vertex count and explicitly leaves the gap to quadratic parameter dependence in the exponent. This is not a super-single-exponential parameter lower bound.

The Journal of the ACM posts Bonnet’s accepted manuscript; the publisher records acceptance on 19 July 2026. These publication dates concern the established exponential lower bound, not a new resolution of the single-exponential parameter question.

sentences: Treewidth is the smallest maximum bag size minus one among tree decompositions of a graph.
The target asks whether ETH rules out exact decision in single-exponential time in the requested width and polynomial time in graph size.
The algorithm must handle every input without receiving a decomposition or a promise that the width threshold is met.
Resolving the question would clarify the cost of discovering the structural information used by many parameterized algorithms.
The new exponential lower bound in the number of vertices is recorded separately because it does not exclude the requested parameter dependence.

definitions: A tree decomposition of \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite nonempty tree \(T\) together with bags \(B_t\subseteq V\) for \(t\in V(T)\), such that every graph vertex belongs to some bag, every edge has both endpoints in one bag, and for each \(v\in V\) the set \(\{t:v\in B_t\}\) induces a connected subtree. Its width is \(\max_t|B_t|-1\), and \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\) is the minimum width over all decompositions. Graphs may be disconnected, with isolated vertices. Their input representation is the binary integer \(n\), the upper-triangular adjacency-bit array on labelled vertices \([n]\), and the binary integer \(k\), using length-delimited fields. The task is exact decision on every input, including graphs with treewidth larger than \(k\); there is no supplied decomposition or promise that the answer is yes. A Turing machine has a fixed finite number of tapes over a fixed finite alphabet, a read-only input tape, initially blank work tapes and a binary output. Each transition moves each head by at most one cell, and all input processing is charged. Programs and constants are uniform in both \(n\) and \(k\); no advice, randomness, oracle or unbounded-precision unit-cost operation is available. The single-exponential class here allows arbitrary constant polynomial factors in \(n\). ETH means that there exists a real \(\delta>0\) such that no deterministic machine in this model decides every 3-CNF formula \(F\) in time \(C\,2^{\delta N}(L+2)^b\) for any fixed \(C\ge1\) and integer \(b\ge1\). Here \(N\ge1\) is the number of Boolean variables, \(L\) is the full binary encoding length, and each clause is a disjunction of at most three literals, each literal being a variable or its negation. The input gives \(N\) in unary and the clauses as length-delimited lists of signed binary variable indices; repeated clauses are permitted. The treewidth and ETH time bounds are worst-case. Exponential dependence on the parameter alone is the target, distinct from an exponential dependence on the entire vertex count.
answer_criterion: Provide a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean, with ETH as the explicit assumption, of either \(\neg\mathrm{FastTW}\) or \(\mathrm{FastTW}\). A proof of impossibility must rule out every constant \(a,b,C\) and every uniform machine meeting the full exact decision specification. A constructive answer must supply such a machine and prove the bound and correctness; an unconditional construction is sufficient for that direction. The accepted theorem must clearly retain its conditional scope and must not claim to establish ETH itself. Ruling out \(2^{o(k)}n^{O(1)}\) time does not rule out \(2^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}\) time. Approximate decompositions, algorithms assuming a decomposition is supplied, or bounds for another problem parameterized by treewidth do not meet this target. This is a binary complexity question, not a numerical approximation of the integer treewidth.

context_blocks.text: Bodlaender’s source asks broadly for time lower bounds and explicitly highlights whether \(2^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}\) time can be ruled out under ETH. The present target retains that conditional single-exponential question, rather than treating any lower bound as a resolution. The exact decision formulation makes the parameter and both yes and no instances explicit.

Korhonen and Lokshtanov improve the exact parameter dependence to \(2^{O(k^2)}n^{O(1)}\), breaking the earlier cubic dependence in the exponent. Their faster approximation result has a different output guarantee. Neither result supplies an exact single-exponential algorithm.

Bonnet establishes an ETH-based \(2^{\Omega(n)}\) lower bound for exact treewidth on \(n\)-vertex graphs. In particular this excludes a subexponential dependence on the treewidth parameter with a polynomial factor in \(n\). It still permits a single-exponential parameterized algorithm, so it does not settle Bodlaender’s explicit example.

The decision formulation is the standard parameterized exact treewidth task. Optimal value computation and finding a suitable decomposition have close algorithmic connections, but the theorem requested here is explicitly about exact decision with a threshold input. It does not impose an additional restriction on polynomial space, polynomial degree or a supplied structural certificate.

The 2026 journal acceptance of Bonnet’s paper confirms publication progress for the lower bound, while its further-work discussion distinguishes the remaining parameter gap. Recent dynamic approximation and algorithms for other tasks on bounded-treewidth graphs address different questions.
